questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To practice the use of German in an academic framework

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I do believe it can be done more effeciently with a greater degree of digitalization, but it was more than sufficient to get started

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Once i had the problem of having my studentcard stolen. That was however no problem and a week afterwards, i had my new one

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky that a familymember was able to offer me housing

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It gives great opportunities to explore the city. Not only you, but also to visit friends you meet, while you are gone

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The system is quite different from what i know, so i had a lot of talks with fellow students to make sure that we got it right and were in fact signing up for classes

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was an event, where we should be there to register and confirm our arrival, with additional informationpapers with access to the different online systems

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a piece of paper with a somewhat thorough description. Also with an email and an office we could contact in case of further questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: My faculty were very cooperative in that sense, that exchangestudents had the right of way. That our picks were valued over the ordinary student. This meant that it was somewhat easy to put together a handful of courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Rather try many differetn courses in the beginnnig, and afterwards narrow yourself down, than being stuck with courses that you thought was something else.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great variation and freedom of choice

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It wasn't always easy to partake orally in the MA-courses in german, but it did up ones understanding of complex and different aspects of my education.A very cool experience

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A different relationship between teacher and student. it definetly had its perks, but you had to figure out how to adress the professor in question, because they prefered different varieties. Sadly i had no lectures and only classes, so i cant comment on how they went

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Hundred Years of Balkan History: The Cases of Montenegro and Bosnia - Johannes Grandits
Geschichte wissenschaftlich schreiben - Philipp Winterhagen
Gesandtschaft und Diplomatie im Spätmittelalter - Dr. Thomas Woelki
Proseminar 'Spaniens Vormachstellung im früneuzeitlichen Europa' - Dr. Tobias Graf
Quellen zum Bauernkrieg - Matthias Pohlig
Empire and British Culture since the 18th Century - Miles Taylor

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Everything with Johannes Grandits as he is a most charismatic teacher. Also to try and experience some of the more niche courses with a focus on specific german history as "Quellen zum Bauernkrieg". You might not be able to contribute that much to the class, but it is a very cool experience to get an understanding of something that to many non-germans, would be a totally new subject

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The exorbitant fees at some of the clubs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The transport was free, as the university had a deal with the BVG. This however seems to be changing so please be aware of this when going there. We werent told to buy any books either, which seems to be the norm in Germany

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Wanted to try and get into soemthing. Never managed or never felt i had the need

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
While the language preparation class was ongoing, there were a lot of opportunities. These ceased by the beginn of the real semester though. There probably was a lot of opportunites, i never managed to take note of them though. 
There should also be a big sportsorganisation, that does all kinds of sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try and experience Berlin for all that it is. Visit museums, Teufelsberg or whatever suits you.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Maybe take a trip to Saxony with Dresden and Leipzig. Or if the weather is any good, go visit one of the lakes where you can go swimming

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: There wanst a great difference from Denmark to Germany and those that where there you should only try to enjoy. Easy transition

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It can be difficult especially if you are only the for one semester

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That Berlin is such a cool city, that you can at times feel like you dont fit in, because you dont follow the "Berlin-vibe".

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The use of public space as an extension of ones home. Especially a warm summer evening

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make sure you have some idea of what your academic interest are, because there are many different courses. And dont be afraid of showing up to a class just to see what it is about.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can also have plenty of experiences, just touring around with fellow ERASMUS-students

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The cool and different people I met, experienced and befriended

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To leave your life back home behind and at times forgetting everything back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
